data.title: Six Flags hits record low as fatal roller coaster raises safety concerns
data.description:
The deadly rollercoaster accident at a Six Flags park in Georgia continues to weigh on the company’s shares, dragging FUN to an all-time low for a fourth straight day in the red.

On Monday, a 42-year-old man fell to his death after being ejected from his seat while on the Goliath hypercoaster at Six Flags Over Georgia. Four children were also injured at the time with non-life-threatening injuries.

The cause of the accident remains under investigation, so it is still too early to determine if it was due to mechanical failure or operational error. As a precaution, Six Flags closed nine rollercoasters in six parks.

While this will have some impact on park attendance, the direct impact on the company’s profit and loss will depend on whether the investigation points to a systemic restraint/design issue or safety failure, UBS advises its clients.

“A key risk for Six Flags is reputational spillover into attendance and pass sales at a time when leverage already limits the company’s ability to absorb a demand shock,” notes UBS analyst Arpine Kocharyab, adding that these types of events are “rare idiosyncratic events” that are unlikely to have a sustained attendance or EBITDA impact.

“Until the investigation establishes root cause, we would view reputational/attendance risk as potentially greater than the direct cost of the Georgia incident itself,” Kocharyab says.

Still, the reputational risk is amplified by a series of events that raise questions over the safety of Six Flags’ rollercoasters.

The parks have been hit with complaints over injuries (some as serious as concussions and dislocated joints), malfunctioning safety restraints, and shoddy maintenance.

In September, a lawsuit representing 100 plaintiffs claims the X2 rollercoaster at Six Flags Magic Mountain in California is linked to numerous injuries, including traumatic brain injuries, and was behind the death of a 22-year-old in June 2022. The lawsuit claims the extreme mechanics of the ride—including 76 mph speed, extreme G-force, and violent jolting—caused the riders’ heads to slam repeatedly against the headrests.

According to an investor lawsuit filed against Six Flags , the company was accused of "failing to make adequate investments to conduct routine facility maintenance or improve rides,” while another federal class-action lawsuit accuses Six Flags’ management of misleading shareholders regarding deferred maintenance and the actual condition of its parks leading into its 2024 merger with Cedar Fair.

Even before the most recent tragic accident, shares of Six Flags were losing ground and have lost more than 60% in value from a year ago.

data.title: Gold set for a weekly drop as traders assess Fed signals
data.description:
Key points:
  • Fed's Warsh mum on rate-path view
  • US PPI and CPI data come in hotter than expected
  • Silver, platinum and palladium head for weekly losses

By Pablo Sinha

Gold prices were largely steady on Friday but were on track for a weekly loss as traders weighed the prospect of further Federal Reserve rate hikes this year following a run of hotter-than-expected US inflation data.

Spot gold was up 0.1% at $4,175.66 per ounce by 11:43 a.m. EDT (1543 GMT) but was down 0.4% so far in the week.

US gold futures for December delivery rose 0.6% to $4,196.40 per ounce.

"We're very much rangebound and tilting toward the lower bound of support, the main reason being we still have a lot of ambiguity in what the Fed will do," Bart Melek, global head of commodity strategy at TD Securities, said.

Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh voiced optimism about US economic strength but gave no clues about the central bank's rate-path trajectory.

Data on Thursday showed US producer prices increased by the most in 4-1/2 years last month. The data followed Wednesday's consumer price report, which showed prices accelerated in September.

Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago President Austan Goolsbee said the data was "discouraging" while Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland President Beth Hammack said the Fed might need to hike interest rates more aggressively if there were to be a notable deterioration in the public's inflation expectations.

Traders largely expect the US central bank to hold rates steady this month, while pricing in a 90% chance of a rate hike in December, according to the CME's FedWatch Tool.

Although gold is typically seen as an inflation hedge, higher interest rates tend to reduce the appeal of the non-yielding metal.

"Over the rest of this year, gold prices are likely to edge lower as the Fed continues raising rates and fears around the end of the AI boom prove to be temporary," Hamad Hussain, a climate and commodities economist at Capital Economics, said.

Elsewhere, gold traded at a premium in India this week for the first time in more than three months as a pullback in prices boosted jewellery purchases.

Among other metals, spot silver was steady at $57.43 per ounce, platinum gained 0.6% to $1,636 and palladium was down 0.2% to $1,124.25. All three metals headed for weekly losses.

data.title: Judge rejects CFTC, Gemini bid to vacate $5 million settlement
data.description:
Key points:
  • Judge says CFTC and Gemini fail to meet standards to set aside settlement
  • January 2025 settlement imposed $5 million civil penalty that Gemini already paid
  • Joint May filing said complaint should not have been filed

By Mike Scarcella

A federal judge in Manhattan has rejected a joint request by the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission and Gemini, a cryptocurrency exchange founded by twin brothers Cameron and Tyler Winklevoss, to undo a $5 million settlement from the Biden administration.

In a ruling on Thursday, US District Judge Alvin Hellerstein said the agency and Gemini Trust Co had not met the standards required to set aside the settlement, which resolved a lawsuit over statements Gemini made during the agency's review of a proposed bitcoin futures contract.

The CFTC and a lawyer for Gemini did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

The CFTC sued Gemini in 2022, alleging the company made false or misleading statements during the agency's review of the proposed futures product. The January 2025 settlement came at the end of Democratic President Joe Biden’s administration and shortly before a trial.

Republican President Donald Trump’s administration has taken a friendlier, narrower approach to crypto sector enforcement.

The commodities agency and Gemini in May jointly asked Hellerstein, appointed by Democratic President Bill Clinton, to wipe out the settlement and court order. They said in a filing that the agency’s complaint, lodged in 2022, would not have been filed under new enforcement policy priorities and standards under Trump.

The court filing said regulators should not ​have accused Gemini of making false statements in connection with ​its bitcoin futures business. The CFTC and Gemini said the CFTC had "resorted to inappropriate tactics" to bring a lawsuit.

Gemini ⁠agreed not to receive a refund on the $5 million penalty if the settlement were vacated.

Hellerstein said Gemini had litigated against the CFTC for more than three years before voluntarily agreeing to settle and that the agency's current view of the case does not require vacating the settlement.

The Winklevoss twins became widely known after accusing Mark Zuckerberg of stealing their idea for Facebook, a dispute that ended with a 2008 settlement that included cash and company stock.

data.title: Bosses Say They Want to Give Employees More Autonomy. But They Don't Act That Way. — WSJ
data.description:
By Sabina Nawaz

Employees say they more want autonomy and bosses say they want to empower the people who report to them. So why does the opposite often happen?

The impasse tends to occur when managers fall into what I call the "sole provider" trap. Worried that their teams are already overburdened or won't do as good a job as they can, these bosses jump in to answer questions, solve problems and take over important tasks before anyone else has a chance to do so.

These bosses usually have good intentions, but by moving fast and responding first they inevitably end up being the team's default problem-solver. It may feel efficient at first but eventually it becomes a burden, leaving managers shouldering too much of the workload and team members waiting for the boss's input before taking action.

How can managers free themselves from this trap and give their employees more autonomy?

Here are three strategies.

1. Set the stage. Empowering employees doesn't mean handing over projects or assignments and letting them figure it all out on their own. If you do that, you might find yourself spending weekends redoing much of the work you thought you had removed from your plate.

So first, lay out clear guidelines, principles and guardrails for the work to help the employee avoid obvious problems and mistakes. That isn't the same as telling employees exactly what to do, which can kill their motivation and creativity. Instead, say things like: "Every proposal you come up with should include three current challenges that your work will address," or "Every solution you propose (the what) should be accompanied by the impact (the so what?)." Providing guidance up front means less work for you and more productivity for the team down the line.

2. Insert a delay window. After setting the stage and giving ownership of a project to a direct report, take a step back. One option is to pause all communication about the project for a set period each day. No email. No chat. No jumping in during that time. This will allow your employees to respond to messages, answer questions, make decisions and solve problems without you hovering in the background. The idea is to give them a window of time to handle things on their own before you make yourself available for questions, coaching or feedback.

3. Ask before you act. Don't assume your employees want to be rescued when work gets especially hectic. For example, you might think you are protecting a direct report's reputation and time by fixing a client proposal or redoing a presentation for the employee. Employees, however, might view it as a lost opportunity to shine or an example of how you don't fully trust him or her to make a decision. So before jumping in, ask your employees what they would find most helpful. Do they want or need you to intervene? Or would they rather you coach them through that stalled proposal or imperfect presentation, so they can build the confidence and skill they need to take on more-challenging work.

In a world where there's too much to do and too little time, giving direct reports more authority helps them grow and expands a team's capacity. It also allows managers to spend more time on what they're uniquely qualified to do, while creating an environment that motivates employees.

data.title: US strikes one-year deal to fund maternal and newborn health donations in poorest countries
data.description:
Key points:
  • Deal covers procurement and delivery of maternal, newborn and nutrition supplies to at least 15 countries for one year
  • UNICEF will take on the US-funded programme, State department says
  • But shortages already an issue in countries like Congo after more than a year of disruption

By Ammu Kannampilly, Jennifer Rigby and Victoire Mukenge

The US government has struck a deal to continue supplying some of the world's poorest nations with free life-saving medication and equipment for mothers, infants and young children, after months of uncertainty and challenges with supply.

The UN children's agency UNICEF will now procure these items, a State department spokesperson told Reuters by email, without giving details of the arrangement. UNICEF said the agreement is worth $25 million and will last for one year.

That sum represents only a small part of the aid affected by the Trump administration's cuts and dismantling of the US Agency for International Development (USAID).

But it means that some of the world's most vulnerable nations will not face another abrupt disruption to supplies they relied on while they work on new health aid deals with the US. Nine former US aid officials, NGOs and government officials told Reuters that this had been a real concern because the deal the now-defunct USAID had with its contractor was due to run out last month.

SHORTAGES

The agreement covers the procurement and delivery of maternal and child health supplies, as well as some nutrition supplies, to at least 15 countries previously covered, including Democratic Republic of Congo, Haiti and Mali, UNICEF said.

It follows almost 18 months of disruption after Washington's move to freeze and then scale back many US aid programmes as part of its "America First Global Health ​Strategy".

In countries such as Congo, shortages due to the disruption have already been showing up on the ground.

At the Nyangezi General Hospital in eastern Congo, health workers said they had run out of supplies of life-saving medications including oxytocin to prevent and treat post-partum haemorrhage and amoxicillin, an antibiotic for paediatric use and during childbirth.

"It was a donation we received (previously) from USAID, and at the moment, there is none," midwife Alice Bulambo told Reuters.

The main government-run warehouse in the area has faced stockouts for over a year, said Olivier Kabarati Amani, chief medical officer for Nyangezi health zone.

As a result, facilities are forced to buy medicines at market prices. Over the last six months, "the cost of care has doubled, if not tripled," Amani said, at a time when the healthcare system in eastern Congo is already struggling with Ebola.

The US State Department said it "has prioritized ensuring all life-saving commodities have continued to be made reliably available."

TRANSITION

Maternal and newborn health items amounted to less than 1% of the more than $5 billion spent by the USAID Global Health Supply Chain program between 2016 and 2023, according to the most recently available annual report. The spending was channelled through private contractor Chemonics.

Reuters first reported on plans to close this programme, which also managed the donation and delivery of supplies to tackle malaria and HIV, in April, with aid officials warning that the September 30 shutdown could cause shortages.

The plans to close the Chemonics supply chain are part of the broader US global health strategy, which aims to move countries towards self-reliance alongside scaled-back US support and reduced reliance on contractors.

The US has instead signed more than 30 bilateral deals on health aid with recipient countries, including Congo, which require co-financing from the countries and are worth billions of dollars in total.

But the details of the deals are still being worked out and it had been unclear what would fill the gap in the ordering procedure in the meantime.

While many nations were already moving towards taking over their maternal and child health needs, lead times for orders can be a year or more, five former USAID officials said.

The Congolese government aims to take over by next year, but has struggled with the recent uncertainty, said Polydor Kabila, coordinator of the universal healthcare programme in the president’s office.

Alongside the UNICEF deal, the US authorities have extended the deadline for Chemonics deliveries of some key malaria and HIV items, the State Department spokesperson told Reuters. The US has also signed a deal with the Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria to allow countries to order new US-funded HIV and malaria supplies through the Fund's order platform.

In a statement, UNICEF said it would work with the US to "keep health and nutrition supplies moving so more children receive life-saving care," adding that no orders have yet been placed but are expected shortly.

data.title: Live entertainment emerging as winner in streaming era
data.description:
Key points:
  • Dow gains, S&P 500 edges down, Nasdaq off >1%
  • Utilities lead S&P 500 sectot gainers; just tech, communication services red
  • Euro STOXX 600 index up ~0.7%
  • Dollar falls; US crude flips green; bitcoin slips; gold up slightly
  • US 10-year Treasury yield flat at ~5.09%

LIVE ENTERTAINMENT EMERGING AS WINNER IN STREAMING ERA

In a digital world where entertainment is just a tap away at home, do people still crave the thrill of live spectacle and value shared experiences?

UBS believes they do. In a recent note, the brokerage said it remains constructive on the long-term outlook for US live entertainment and sports, with both categories growing faster than total personal consumption expenditures (PCE).

In the second quarter of 2026, spending on live entertainment rose 15% year-over-year, while spectator sports spending climbed more than 20%, far outpacing PCE growth of roughly 6%, according to US Bureau of Economic Analysis data.

The combined US spending on live entertainment and spectator sports now exceeds $100 billion annually.

"We expect the category to continue outpacing overall household spending over the medium term, supported by pricing power, premiumization, sponsorship growth, media monetization, and related travel expenditures," UBS said.

The audience profile is another tailwind. Live-event consumers tend to be younger and more affluent demographics that have historically shown stronger spending power and more durable demand, the brokerage noted.

UBS also points to broader cultural changes. Streaming has created a richer and more diverse entertainment landscape, but one that is less universally shared. With fewer people watching the same shows and films together, consumers may be placing greater value on real-world shared experiences.

The brokerage notes that trend has also been reflected in media stocks. IMAX dramatically outperformed Netflix over the past year, with the cinema operator rising about 45% in 2025, compared with a little more than 5% for the streaming giant. The divergence continued in 2026.

Among public companies, UBS highlighted Live Nation as the dominant player in the live-entertainment industry and Sphere Entertainment , whose Las Vegas Sphere venue represents an emerging immersive-entertainment model, as among beneficiaries of growing demand for event-style entertainment.

data.title: ImmunityBio Reports Phase 3 Data Showing 84% Cystectomy Avoidance at Three Years and Complete Responses Beyond 53 Months with ANKTIVA® Plus BCG in BCG-Unresponsive NMIBC With CIS, With or Without Papillary Tumors
data.description:
ImmunityBio, Inc. (), a commercial-stage immunotherapy company, today announced the publication of long-term data from the Phase 2/3 QUILT-3.032 study (N=100) in the Journal of Urology. The study evaluated ANKTIVA® (nogapendekin alfa inbakicept-pmln) in combination with Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) in patients with BCG-unresponsive non-muscle invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) with carcinoma in situ (CIS), with or without papillary disease.

Highlights:

  • 71% complete response (CR) rate in patients with BCG-unresponsive NMIBC CIS, with or without papillary disease

  • Median duration of CR of 26.6 months, with responses extending beyond 53 months

  • More than half of responding patients in the FDA-reviewed population maintained complete responses beyond 45 months

  • 84% cystectomy-free survival at 36 months among responders

  • 98.2% disease-specific survival at three years

  • No Grade 4 or Grade 5 treatment-related adverse events reported

“The QUILT-3.032 study represents one of the longest follow-up data sets in BCG-unresponsive NMIBC to date, and the results continue to support the durability of ANKTIVA’s unique mechanism of action in generating sustained immune responses,” said Patrick Soon-Shiong, M.D., Founder, Executive Chairman and Global Chief Scientific and Medical Officer of ImmunityBio. “These long-term findings are encouraging, suggesting the potential for prolonged disease control and the possibility of avoiding or delaying radical cystectomy for some patients.”

The publication also reported:

  • 63.8% of responders maintained CR for at least 12 months

  • 52.3% maintained CR for at least 24 months

  • 44.2% maintained CR for at least 36 months

  • Progression-free survival remained 80.9% at three years

  • In BCG refractory (never responded) patients, the CR rate was 66%

  • 4% of responders progressed to muscle-invasive disease

The treatment continued to demonstrate a favorable safety profile. Most treatment-related adverse events were Grade 1 or Grade 2 and consisted of localized bladder symptoms associated with intravesical therapy. Grade 3 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 4% of patients, with no Grade 4 or Grade 5 treatment-related adverse events reported.

“Achieving a durable response and avoiding cystectomy are important treatment goals for patients with BCG-unresponsive NMIBC,” said Richard Adcock, President and CEO of ImmunityBio. “These peer-reviewed results add to the growing body of evidence supporting ANKTIVA plus BCG and highlight its potential to provide sustained disease control and meaningful cystectomy avoidance for patients with limited treatment options. We thank the patients and clinical teams who contributed to this long-term follow-up.”

The publication builds upon the growing body of clinical evidence supporting ANKTIVA plus BCG, which was initially approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) in 2024 for the treatment of adult patients with BCG-unresponsive NMIBC with CIS, with or without papillary tumors. In October 2026, the FDA expanded the approved indication to include patients with BCG-unresponsive NMIBC with papillary-only disease. ANKTIVA is the first FDA-approved IL-15 receptor agonist and the first approved immunotherapy in NMIBC designed to activate natural killer (NK) cells and T cells to generate durable immune responses.

About the QUILT 3.032 Study

QUILT-3.032 (NCT03022825) is a multicenter Phase 2/3 study evaluating ANKTIVA plus BCG in patients with BCG-unresponsive NMIBC. The published analysis includes 100 patients with CIS with or without papillary disease and represents one of the longest follow-up datasets reported in this disease setting, with outcomes extending beyond five years in some patients.

About ANKTIVA® (nogapendekin alfa inbakicept-pmln)

The interleukin-15 (IL-15) cytokine plays a crucial role in the immune system by affecting the development, maintenance, and function of key immune cells—NK and CD8+ killer T cells—that are involved in killing cancer cells. By activating NK cells, ANKTIVA® overcomes the tumor escape phase of clones resistant to T cells and restores memory T cell activity with resultant prolonged duration of complete response. data.title: MHI Delivers Three Replacement Steam Generators for EDF's Nuclear Power Plant
data.description:
TOKYO, Oct 16, 2026 - (JCN Newswire) - Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, Ltd. (MHI) has completed the delivery of three replacement steam generators (SGs) to Electricite de France S.A. (EDF, headquartered in Paris) for its nuclear power plant in France. Manufacturing of these replacement SGs was completed at MHI's Kobe facility (Hyogo-ku, Kobe) in January 2024. At the end of February this year, they obtained a certificate complying with strict standards required by the French nuclear regulatory authority, and were subsequently transported to France. MHI has received orders for a total of 9 replacement SGs from EDF, and the remaining 6 units are currently being manufactured at MHI's Kobe facilities, with delivery scheduled from 2028 onwards.

EDF ordered the newly delivered replacement SGs in 2019 from both MHI and Onet Technologies(1) for a 900 MWe pressurized water reactor (PWR) nuclear power plant. They are scheduled to be installed in Unit 2 of the Cruas Nuclear Power Plant, located in the Ardeche department of southeastern France.

SGs are among the most important components of PWR plants, transferring the thermal energy generated in the reactor vessel from the primary cooling system (reactor system) to the secondary cooling system (turbine system) to generate steam to drive the turbine. Each SG measures approximately 21 meters in height and has a total weight of around 330 tons. Approximately 4,500 heat transfer tubes made of TT690 alloy(2), which feature high corrosion resistance, are inserted into a pressure-resistant vessel made of low-alloy steel(3).

MHI has delivered a cumulative total of 15 replacement SGs to EDF since 2005, excluding those delivered this time. EDF is one of the world's largest power utilities, operating 57 PWR plants in France. In accordance with French government policy to extend the operating life of nuclear power plants beyond 40 years, EDF had been progressively replacing SGs at its PWR plants that started operation in the 1980s. As France continues to strengthen its nuclear regulatory requirements, the successful delivery of replacement SGs that fully comply with the regulations demonstrates that MHI's technological expertise, manufacturing quality, reliability, and capability to adapt to French standards and regulations are highly regarded.

MHI has a proven track record of delivering more than 30 replacement SGs to overseas countries including France, Belgium, and the United States. MHI has received orders for more than 130 SGs in total, including both new installations and replacements projects in Japan. MHI continues to contribute to extending the operating life, as well as enhancing the safety and economic efficiency, of PWR plants both in Japan and globally.

From the point of view of carbon neutrality and energy security, there has been a rise in demand for utilization of nuclear power around the world. MHI will continue to contribute to the safe and stable operation of nuclear power plants by supplying products requiring high reliability to both the domestic and overseas nuclear markets, including France. In addition, through the manufacturing of replacement SGs, MHI will pass on the comprehensive technological capabilities it has cultivated over many years as a nuclear power plant manufacturer to the next generation, while continuing to supply high-quality equipment from Kobe to the world.

(1) Headquartered in Marseille, France, Onet Technologies specializes in providing professional maintenance and support services for nuclear facilities and has been in partnership with MHI since 2002.(2) TT690 is a nickel, chromium, and iron alloy that has been specially heat-treated to enhance corrosion resistance. It is used as the material for SG heat transfer tubes, offering superior corrosion resistance under high-temperature and high-pressure conditions.(3) Low-alloy steel refers to steel containing 5% or less of alloying elements. SGs are manufactured as pressure-resistant vessels using strong low-alloy steel (manganese-molybdenum-nickel steel).

Mitsubishi Heavy Industries (MHI) Group is one of the world's leading industrial groups, spanning energy, smart infrastructure, industrial machinery, aerospace and defense. data.title: Hop-On's Digitalage Demonstrates Governed AI Newsroom Infrastructure From Source to Delivery
data.description:
Working pilot is designed to preserve source traceability, editorial approval, production state, quality controls, catalog identity and delivery history across an automated media workflow

TEMECULA, CA / ACCESS Newswire / October 16, 2026 / Hop-on, Inc. today announced that its wholly owned subsidiary, Digitalage, Inc., has developed a working pilot console for its AI-assisted news-video infrastructure, demonstrating an end-to-end workflow that moves source material through editorial review, video production, quality control, cataloging and delivery.

The pilot advances Digitalage beyond individual media-generation tools toward a broader operating layer designed for publishers, news organizations, communications companies and enterprises that need to produce media at scale while preserving source traceability, editorial control and an operating record.

Digitalage is building around the full media lifecycle:

INGEST. VERIFY. PRODUCE. REVIEW. GOVERN. DELIVER.

Peter Michaels, Chairman and CEO of Hop-on, Inc. and Founder and Chairman of Digitalage, said:

"This is exactly what I mean when I say Digitalage is infrastructure, not another AI video generator."

"Generating a video is the easy part. The bigger problem is everything around it. Where did the story come from? What source supports it? Who approved it? Did it pass quality review? Can it be changed without rebuilding everything? Where was it delivered? Can you prove what happened?"

"Anyone can push a button and make a video. We are building the infrastructure behind the button."

THREE PATHS FROM SOURCE TO VIDEO

The current pilot demonstrates three distinct production workflows.

The first allows an authorized user to provide source text and produce a video using an AI presenter.

The second allows incoming feed content to trigger production automatically through configurable rules, allowing those rules to determine whether material proceeds through the workflow without manual intervention.

The third provides an editorially controlled path in which a proposed script is checked against its underlying source material and held for human approval before rendering begins.

Together, those workflows are intended to allow organizations to automate routine production without surrendering editorial authority when human review is required.

AN OPERATING SYSTEM AROUND THE MEDIA

The working pilot brings multiple production, editorial and governance functions into a unified console.

Capabilities demonstrated by the Digitalage development team include:

  • Source-text and feed-based story ingestion
  • AI-presenter video generation
  • Rule-based automated processing
  • Source-to-script editorial review
  • Human approval before rendering
  • A 14-stage rendering workflow
  • A 71-check video quality report
  • Story and editorial management
  • Feed and automation-rule management
  • Media cataloging
  • Reusable brand kits
  • Signed webhook delivery
  • Per-run API capability validation and usage tracking

The system currently includes 87 working API capabilities.

The console tracks which capabilities are exercised and validated during each individual workflow run. Accordingly, a display such as "4 of 87" reflects the number of capabilities used or validated in that specific run, not the number of capabilities available or functioning across the system.

Automated testing, engineering review, improvements and bug fixes continue across the platform.

Digitalage is developing the architecture as a multi-vendor environment rather than one dependent on a single AI model or provider.

The objective is infrastructure capable of orchestrating the tools each workflow requires.

AUTOMATION WITHOUT REMOVING ACCOUNTABILITY

Digitalage believes artificial intelligence will dramatically increase the speed and volume at which media can be created.

The company also believes greater automation makes provenance, source traceability, editorial controls and auditable production processes more important, not less.

The Digitalage architecture is being designed so routine workflows can be automated while organizations retain human approval where editorial policy requires it.

The system is also being developed to preserve underlying source material and production state so changes can be made within the workflow rather than forcing an editor to rebuild an entire production from the beginning.

Robert T. Braun, CEO of Digitalage, said:

"Enterprise customers do not simply need another tool that can generate content. They need reliability, repeatability, governance, control and an operating record."

"As these systems scale, the value is not simply in creating another piece of media. It is in maintaining the source, rights, editorial decisions, production state and delivery history around that media."

"That is what turns a collection of AI tools into enterprise infrastructure."

THE MEDIA KEEPS ITS HISTORY

Most generative tools are designed to produce an output.

Digitalage is being developed around a different model:

The finished media should retain an operating record of how it came into existence.

That record is designed to include the underlying source material, script development, editorial decisions, approval state, production stages, quality review, catalog identity and delivery history.

The objective is to allow an organization to know not only what was published, but also how it got there.

That distinction becomes increasingly important as organizations move from manually producing individual pieces of content to using artificial intelligence and automation to produce media at scale.

Michaels said:

"A finished video should not become a dead file the moment it is rendered."

"We want the source, the decisions, the approvals, the production history and the delivery record to remain connected to the media."

"Most AI tools give you an output. We are building infrastructure that remembers how the output was created."

ONE INFRASTRUCTURE LAYER ACROSS THE MEDIA LIFECYCLE

The news-video console is part of a broader Digitalage architecture being developed across live broadcasting, replay, recorded media, creator monetization, moderation, provenance, searchable catalogs, AI-assisted publishing, rights-aware workflows and enterprise licensing.

Digitalage is also being designed to work alongside production tools creators already use.

Rather than requiring creators to abandon established broadcasting workflows or audiences, Digitalage is designed to accept streams through workflows compatible with production environments such as OBS.

The strategy is straightforward:

CREATORS SHOULD NOT HAVE TO START OVER SIMPLY TO ADD DIGITALAGE.

OBS functions as a production control room where creators can manage cameras, audio and graphics before sending a live stream to an audience.

Digitalage's stream-key workflow is designed to allow creators to add Digitalage alongside existing broadcast channels rather than requiring them to replace those channels.

Digitalage's creator application, currently in testing, connects multiple portions of this lifecycle, including live broadcasting, replay, timed interaction, catalogs and access-pass payment functionality.

When a live event ends, the Digitalage model is designed to continue.

The live stream can become a replay.

The replay can become part of the creator's catalog.

Conversation can remain connected to the moment that created it.

The resulting media can continue creating opportunities for discovery, access and monetization.

The same architectural philosophy now extends into news production.

A story can begin as source material, move through structured editorial and production stages, become finished media and enter a persistent catalog rather than existing only as a one-time AI render.

Digitalage summarizes the model with a simple principle:

"Live is the moment. The catalog is the business."

FROM WORKING PILOT TO COMMERCIAL DEPLOYMENT

With the core workflow now demonstrated, Digitalage's next phase is focused on converting the pilot into deployable enterprise infrastructure.

Current work includes production hardening, performance testing, determining finished-media production costs, configuring customer-specific workflows, establishing pricing and finalizing commercial billing architecture for the newsroom product.

The current news-video pilot operates on a local development stack, and certain production components remain under continuous review, testing and development.

Digitalage is not announcing commercial revenue or a completed customer deployment from the newsroom pilot at this time.

The company intends to demonstrate the system to prospective publishers, news organizations, communications companies and enterprise customers as development reaches the appropriate stage.

Signed commercial agreements and deployments will be announced when and if they are finalized.

The objective is now to move from demonstrated technology to controlled commercial deployment.

DIGITALAGE: NOT A PLATFORM. INFRASTRUCTURE.

Digitalage's development work now spans multiple interconnected layers of the media lifecycle, including live broadcasting, replay, VOD, creator access and monetization, moderation, content processing, searchable media, AI-assisted production and enterprise workflows.

Rather than developing isolated applications for each media format or tying the company's future to a single artificial-intelligence provider, Digitalage is pursuing an infrastructure model in which live, recorded, human-created and AI-assisted media can operate through a shared underlying architecture.

Michaels concluded:

"We spent years building pieces of this architecture. Now those pieces are beginning to work together."

"Live. Replay. Verification. Moderation. News production. Rights. Delivery. Monetization."

"Not a platform. Infrastructure."

ABOUT HOP-ON, INC.

Hop-on, Inc. is a publicly traded technology company and the parent company of Digitalage, Inc.

Through Digitalage, the company is developing stateful media infrastructure for live and recorded content, creator media, publishing workflows, provenance, content governance, searchable catalogs, rights-aware distribution and monetization.

data.title: Seagate and Western Digital Stocks Fall on Toshiba Fears. Wells Fargo Is Still Bullish. — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Ty Roush

Shares of hard-drive makers Seagate Technology and Western Digital have come under pressure as concerns mount about growing competition from Toshiba. But Wells Fargo says the selloff has been exaggerated.

Seagate fell 4.9% to $657.41 on Friday, while Western Digital dropped 4.6% to $339.84. The stocks are down 27% and 24% in October, respectively, and both have fallen 14% over their current five-day losing streaks, according to Dow Jones Market Data.

Wells Fargo analysts maintained Overweight ratings for Seagate and Western Digital in a note Friday, even as they slashed their price targets for both stocks. They lowered their Seagate target to $865 from $1,180, and Western Digital to $450 from $730. Those freshly cut targets still represent upsides of 26% and 25% from the stocks' closing prices on Thursday, respectively.

This month's declines for Seagate and Western Digital — which came after a report indicated Japanese rival Toshiba plans to double its hard-drive production capacity — have been "well overdone," the analysts said, calling Toshiba's execution "a prove-it story." Toshiba declined to comment to Barron's about the report at the time.

The analysts disputed a Nikkei report suggesting Toshiba could claim 30% of the hard-drive market by fiscal 2027, arguing that even doubling its production capacity would support only a midteens market share at best.

Investors also might have overestimated how much additional supply Toshiba plans to bring to market. Wells Fargo analysts noted that a revised report from Nikkei clarified Toshiba intends to double production capacity from fiscal 2025 levels, not fiscal 2026, as investors initially assumed. The analysts estimate the distinction represents a difference of 70 to 90 million terabytes of storage capacity.

As for the outlook for Seagate and Western Digital, their gross margins are expected to approach 70% by 2028, the analysts said. They cited continued price increases, lower production costs, and tight industry supply as key drivers of profitability.

Wells Fargo expects Western Digital's annual revenue to grow to $29.1 billion in 2028 from $15.8 billion in fiscal 2026, while Seagate's revenue is projected to climb to $28.2 billion from $15.3 billion over the same period.

Both stocks have jumped considerably this year, regardless of their recent drops. Seagate has surged 143% in 2026, while Western Digital has risen 99%. The companies have become two of the largest beneficiaries of the AI boom as they reap the rewards of growing demand for data storage.

data.title: US agrees one-year deal to fund maternal and newborn health donations in poorest countries
data.description:
Key points:
  • Deal covers procurement and delivery of maternal, newborn and nutrition supplies to at least 15 countries for one year
  • UNICEF will take on the US-funded programme, State department says
  • But shortages already an issue in countries like Congo after more than a year of disruption

By Ammu Kannampilly, Jennifer Rigby and Victoire Mukenge

The US government has struck a deal to continue supplying some of the world's poorest nations with free life-saving medication and equipment for mothers, infants and young children, after months of uncertainty and challenges with supply.

The UN children's agency UNICEF will now procure these items, a State department spokesperson told Reuters by email, without giving details of the arrangement. UNICEF said the agreement is worth $25 million and will last for one year.

That sum represents only a small part of the aid affected by the Trump administration's cuts and dismantling of the US Agency for International Development (USAID).

But it means that some of the world's most vulnerable nations will not face another abrupt disruption to supplies they relied on while they work on new health aid deals with the US. Nine former US aid officials, NGOs and government officials told Reuters that this had been a real concern because the deal the now-defunct USAID had with its contractor was due to run out last month.

SHORTAGES

The agreement covers the procurement and delivery of maternal and child health supplies, as well as some nutrition supplies, to at least 15 countries previously covered, including Democratic Republic of Congo, Haiti and Mali, UNICEF said.

It follows almost 18 months of disruption after Washington's move to freeze and then scale back many US aid programmes as part of its "America First Global Health ​Strategy".

In countries such as Congo, shortages due to the disruption have already been showing up on the ground.

At the Nyangezi General Hospital in eastern Congo, health workers said they had run out of supplies of life-saving medications including oxytocin to prevent and treat post-partum haemorrhage and amoxicillin, an antibiotic for paediatric use and during childbirth.

"It was a donation we received (previously) from USAID, and at the moment, there is none," midwife Alice Bulambo told Reuters.

The main government-run warehouse in the area has faced stockouts for over a year, said Olivier Kabarati Amani, chief medical officer for Nyangezi health zone.

As a result, facilities are forced to buy medicines at market prices. Over the last six months, "the cost of care has doubled, if not tripled," Amani said, at a time when the healthcare system in eastern Congo is already struggling with Ebola.

The US State Department said it "has prioritized ensuring all life-saving commodities have continued to be made reliably available."

TRANSITION

Maternal and newborn health items amounted to less than 1% of the more than $5 billion spent by the USAID Global Health Supply Chain program between 2016 and 2023, according to the most recently available annual report. The spending was channelled through private contractor Chemonics.

Reuters first reported on plans to close this programme, which also managed the donation and delivery of supplies to tackle malaria and HIV, in April, with aid officials warning that the September 30 shutdown could cause shortages.

The plans to close the Chemonics supply chain are part of the broader US global health strategy, which aims to move countries towards self-reliance alongside scaled-back US support and reduced reliance on contractors.

The US has instead signed more than 30 bilateral deals on health aid with recipient countries, including Congo, which require co-financing from the countries and are worth billions of dollars in total.

But the details of the deals are still being worked out and it had been unclear what would fill the gap in the ordering procedure in the meantime.

While many nations were already moving towards taking over their maternal and child health needs, lead times for orders can be a year or more, five former USAID officials said.

The Congolese government aims to take over by next year, but has struggled with the recent uncertainty, said Polydor Kabila, coordinator of the universal healthcare programme in the president’s office.

Alongside the UNICEF deal, the US authorities have extended the deadline for Chemonics deliveries of some key malaria and HIV items, the State Department spokesperson told Reuters. The US has also signed a deal with the Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria to allow countries to order new US-funded HIV and malaria supplies through the Fund's order platform.

In a statement, UNICEF said it would work with the US to "keep health and nutrition supplies moving so more children receive life-saving care," adding that no orders have yet been placed but are expected shortly.

data.title: FPIs will return to Indian equities despite sustained outflows: HDFC AMC CEO
data.description:
Mumbai, Oct. 16 -- Foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) will eventually return as net buyers of Indian equities despite sustained selling in recent months, as the country's long-term economic fundamentals remain strong, HDFC Asset Management Company Managing Director and CEO Navneet Munot said on Friday.

His remarks come amid continued foreign investor withdrawals from Indian equities, driven by elevated global interest rates, high crude oil prices and concerns over emerging market investments.

Speaking on the sidelines of the listing of the HDFC FTSE India Equity ETF at the National Stock Exchange (NSE) in Mumbai, Munot said foreign investors continued to show interest in select investment opportunities, including initial public offerings (IPOs), even as overall flows remained negative.

"We have seen FPI outflows over the last several quarters. But you can also see their interest in several of the IPOs, where foreign portfolio investors have participated. In between, there were times when foreign portfolio investors were investing," Munot said.

"India's long-term fundamentals remain intact, and I remain confident that at some stage, FPIs will be net buyers again," he added.

Foreign investors had withdrawn Rs 44,166 crore from Indian equities in October up to October 11, taking their total outflows in 2026 to more than Rs 3 lakh crore, according to NSDL data.

The continued selling has weighed on market sentiment even as domestic institutional investors have remained an important source of support for Indian equities.

Meanwhile, HDFC Mutual Fund listed its FTSE India Equity ETF on the NSE on Friday, expanding its range of passive investment products.

The exchange-traded fund tracks the FTSE India Equity Index, which provides diversified exposure to large- and mid-cap Indian stocks.

"Their index comprises 272 stocks - it's a very diversified index. We will be giving an opportunity to domestic investors to participate in an index which has been provided by a globally recognized index provider. Over a period of time, we can also showcase this strategy to global investors," Munot said.

The ETF aims to provide investors with exposure to a broad segment of India's listed equity market through a single investment product.

data.title: Yes Bank’s CET1 ratio to take 250-basis-point hit after AT1 bond ruling
data.description:
Following the Supreme Court upholding the 2023 Bombay High Court judgment quashing the write-down of Additional Tier (AT)-1 Bonds aggregating ₹8,415 crore by Yes Bank, the Bank said the pro forma impact of reinstatement of these Bonds’ principal amount on Common Equity Tier (CET) 1 Ratio (including profits) as on June 30, 2026 is expected to be 250 basis points.

However, the Tier-1 Ratio on a pro forma basis will remain unchanged at 14 per cent.

In a regulatory filing, the Bank said it is examining the Supreme Court judgment in detail, including evaluating all available legal options and suitable actions/steps going forward.

Yes Bank emphasised that it has access to appropriate capital-management levers and can undertake additional capital actions, as it deems appropriate, to pursue its growth objectives.

S&P says Yes Bank can withstand capital impact

S&P Global Ratings assessed that Yes Bank‘s credit profile can withstand the Supreme Court of India’s ruling that the write-off of its additional Tier 1 (AT1) bonds was illegal.

The agency underscored that Yes Bank’s regulatory capital is adequate. As of the end of March 2026, the bank’s CET1 ratio stood at a healthy 13.87%, providing a significant cushion. It said. This will allow the bank to absorb an anticipated 250 basis-point impact on its CET1 while remaining well above the minimum regulatory requirement of 5.5%

“In our view, this ruling relates to procedures that Yes Bank did not follow under the reconstruction scheme exercised during the 2020 rescue. The Supreme Court decision is seen as addressing the procedural lapses in the write-down process rather than questioning the instrument’s fundamental loss-absorbing characteristics,” the rating agency said.

S&P noted that “it is unclear whether Yes Bank will challenge the ruling, however, if enforced, we do not expect it to affect our ratings on the bank.”

AT1 bonds are designed to absorb losses

Under the Basel III framework, AT1 instruments are specifically designed to absorb losses through either conversion into common equity or a write-down mechanism once a pre-specified trigger point is met.

In India, this trigger typically occurs when the common equity Tier 1 (CET1) ratio falls below 6.125% of risk-weighted assets, or when regulators determine the issuer is no longer viable.

Capital ratios expected to remain adequate

S&P expects Yes Bank to remain adequately capitalised, with its risk-adjusted capital (RAC) ratio projected to stay within the 8.0%-8.5% range through the fiscal years ending March 31, 2027 and 2028, compared with 9.0% as of March 2026.

“We do not anticipate any meaningful impact on our total adjusted capital (the numerator for our RAC ratio calculation). We expect the negative impact of approximately Indian rupee (INR) 84 billion (Rs 8,400 crore) to common equity to be largely offset by the reinstatement of the AT1 instruments to a similar extent. Going forward, we see this as earnings negative as the AT1’s has high coupon payments of 9.0%-9.5%,” the agency said.

Coupon payments remain a key uncertainty

The Supreme Court order states that the coupon rate will remain unaffected by the outcome of the appeals and must be made in terms of the information memoranda.

“Like other AT1s, Yes Bank’s AT1 also allows for discretionary coupon payments; however, it is unclear if the bank will pay coupons for the 5.5-year intervening period. We note that Dhanalaxmi Bank Ltd. was permitted to defer coupon payments on its Basel II-compliant Tier II instruments, demonstrating the loss-absorption potential of such hybrid debt.

“We currently do not expect material impact of this on the bank’s credit profile but will continue to monitor any related developments. Yes Bank last paid a dividend on its common equity in 2019,” S&P said.

data.title: Canada, India aim to conclude CEPA by year-end; Fairfax deal signals investment momentum
data.description:
India and Canada are on track to conclude negotiations for a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) by the end of this year, with the next round of talks scheduled for the week of November 9 in India, Canadian International Trade Minister Maninder Sidhu said on Friday.

“We've completed five rounds. We're going to be doing another round on the week of November 9 back here in India,” Sidhu said at a press conference in Bengaluru, as Canada concluded its largest trade mission to India in three decades.

Pointing to Fairfax Financial Holdings’ acquisition of a majority stake in IDBI Bank in a deal valued at nearly C$8 billion, Sidhu said the transaction reflected growing investor confidence in India and could encourage further investment. He noted that Fairfax had already invested significantly in India, including in Bengaluru International Airport.

The deal, he said, sent a “clear signal to the supply chains that Canada is ready to do more”.

Expand exposure

Canadian pension funds and large institutions have collectively invested close to C$107 billion in India across sectors including roads, highways, healthcare, technology, clean technology and energy, Sidhu said, adding that investors were looking to expand their exposure.

The trade mission brought 300 business delegates representing 150 organisations to India. More than 30 deals between Canadian delegates and Indian partners, valued at nearly C$300 million, were recorded during the visit, he said.

The sectors represented opportunities for deeper collaboration in energy, critical minerals, fertilisers, aerospace, artificial intelligence, quantum computing and data centres. Sidhu said Canadian fertiliser exports to India had grown 85 per cent over recent years, while aerospace exports rose 300 per cent last year.

The two countries are seeking to more than double bilateral trade to C$70 billion by 2030, with the proposed CEPA expected to improve market access for businesses on both sides.

data.title: Ola Electric’s ₹1,000 crore rights issue uncovers SEBI scrutiny, audit deficiencies
data.description:
Ola Electric is seeking nearly ₹1,000 crore from shareholders even as the electric two-wheeler maker and its founder, Bhavish Aggarwal, face a pending SEBI proceeding over allegedly misleading public disclosures. The company’s rights offer also reveals that auditors flagged the absence of mandatory internal audit systems at the company and two subsidiaries during FY26.

Against this backdrop, Aggarwal recently announced another distribution push.

“What energy our dealers have! First 150 onboarded, and it was amazing to host and interact with them in our factory!” he said in a social media communication reproduced in Ola’s October 9 stock exchange filing. The announcement did not specify how many dealer outlets were operational or their servicing capabilities.

Seeds of doubts

Kranthi Bathini, Director – Equity Strategy at WealthMills Securities, said the company’s statements and regulatory disclosures had created doubts among investors about the credibility of management communications, leaving them uncertain about what to believe or trust when management makes public announcements.

The concerns assume significance because Ola’s earlier network claims are under regulatory scrutiny. The offer document records a January 7, 2025, SEBI administrative warning after Aggarwal announced a fourfold expansion of company-owned stores on social media before informing the stock exchanges. The latest dealer communication, however, was disclosed to the bourses.

Orders or sales?

SEBI’s April 10 show-cause notice concerns Ola’s February 2025 announcement that it had sold more than 25,000 electric vehicles during the month.

According to the offer document, SEBI alleged that “the disclosed figure represented confirmed orders rather than completed sales involving registration and delivery”. It also questioned disclosures concerning payments, cancellations and fulfilment, alleging that only a portion translated into registrations and recognised revenue.

Ola subsequently clarified that the figure referred to bookings rather than recorded sales.

In Risk Factor 53, the company states: “We track certain operational metrics with internal systems and tools and do not independently verify such metrics.” These include sales volumes, order fulfilment and after-sales service volumes. Ola maintains that its reported metrics are accurate.

Disclosures questioned

SEBI’s notice also alleges misleading December 2024 announcements about more than 3,200 stores being co-located with service centres and an expansion to 4,000 stores. The regulator alleged that these disclosures contributed to an 8.45 per cent increase in Ola’s share price on December 2, 2024.

The notice further questions Roadster and Roadster X motorcycle prototype approvals and delivery timelines.

The offer document states that SEBI alleged Aggarwal “disseminated or was responsible for misleading public statements and corporate announcements and incorrectly certified matters relating to financial reporting and internal controls”.

Ola and Aggarwal filed a settlement application on June 8, 2026. It remained pending as of October 7. The allegations have not been established through a final regulatory order.

Control gaps

Separately, auditors reported that Ola Electric Mobility, Ola Cell Technologies and Ola Electric Technologies lacked mandatory internal audit systems during FY26. The consolidated internal financial controls report also contained a qualified opinion concerning inventory-verification controls at a subsidiary.

The ₹999.74-crore rights issue follows Ola’s ₹5,500-crore IPO in 2024 and ₹780.24-crore institutional placement in June 2026. The offer acknowledges that proceeds from earlier issues remain partly unutilised, while the latest fundraising covers overlapping purposes, including debt repayment, organic growth and general corporate expenditure.

Priced at ₹27 a share, the issue has an October 13 record date and runs from October 22 to 30. Aggarwal has pledged shares representing 4.32 per cent of Ola’s equity to finance his participation, according to the filing.

data.title: Tractor retail sales rise 13.7% YoY in September on low base effect
data.description:
India’s tractor retail sales rose 13.7 per cent year-on-year in September 2026 to 76,906 units from 67,612 units a year earlier with the relatively lower base of September 2025 given the implementation of GST 2.0, according to data from the Federation of Automobile Dealers Associations (FADA).

Tractor sales in September 2026, however, declined 12.6 per cent month-on-month amid a late festive calendar and patchy monsoon conditions.

Mahindra & Mahindra (M&M) and its Swaraj division together accounting for nearly 42 per cent of the market, as per FADA data.

Most key manufacturers reported YoY growth in September with International Tractors Ltdreported the highest growth with 27.1 per cent.

The year-on-year growth in September needs to be interpreted with caution, as last year’s base was influenced by buyers postponing purchases ahead of the GST rate reduction, Poonam Upadhyay, Director, Crisil Ratings, said.

“The September [MoM] dip in tractor retail sales appears more a matter of timing than shift in underlying demand. Unlike most automobile segments, over 80 per cent of tractor sales are linked to rural markets, where purchase decisions are often aligned with auspicious periods and harvest-linked cash flows,” she said. With the festive season shifting into October this year, part of September demand appears to have been deferred, she added.

Escorts Kubota Limited Agri Machinery Business said that looking ahead, festive demand, crop harvesting and improving rural liquidity are expected to support industry volumes. However, the high base effect may continue to moderate industry growth in the near term.

data.title: Urban Company net loss widens in Q2, revenue up 41.4%
data.description:
Home services platform, Urban Company Ltd widened its consolidated net loss to ₹182.48 crore in Q2 FY27 compared to ₹59.33 crore in the year-ago period as it continued aggressive investments in InstaHelp. Consolidated revenue from operations grew 41.4 per cent to ₹537.29 crore. The company’s board also approved raising up to ₹2,500 crore through the issue of equity shares or other convertible securities via qualified institutional placement (QIP), subject to shareholder approval.

In the shareholders’ letter, the company’s management said, “Q2 FY27 was a strong quarter for Urban Company with continued growth momentum and margin expansion for our core business. At the same time, we continued to invest aggressively in InstaHelp, where unit economics improved despite rapid scale-up.”

On a consolidated basis, net transaction value (NTV) grew 39 per cent y-o-y to ₹1,432 crore. Orders delivered reached 15.1 million, up 103 per cent y-o-y, and annual transacting users reached nearly 10 million, up 35 per cent y-o-y it added.

On the proposed fundraise, the company said, “We are on track to achieve our targets, and are raising capital for strategic flexibility. We closed the quarter with ₹1,901 crore in cash and treasury investment. The business is materially larger than at listing, growth has stepped up, and we now operate three businesses at scale with proven economics.”

‘On track’

“The proposed raise of up to ₹2,500 crore is about flexibility: it lets us invest with conviction across each of them, cement leadership in InstaHelp, and pursue inorganic opportunities selectively, without trading off one for another. We remain on track for adjusted EBITDA break-even by Q3 FY28 and Adjusted EBITDA of ₹1,000 crore by FY31,” it added in its filing.

Revenue from India consumer services business, excluding InstaHelp, rose 28.4 per cent to ₹336.38 crore.

The company’s InstaHelp business, which offers households daily cleaning and housekeeping needs, reported a segment loss of ₹173.12 crore in the quarter, compared with ₹42.91 crore loss a year ago, according to the filing. The segment revenue rose to ₹20.54 crore in Q2 FY27 from ₹1.43 crore in Q2 FY26. Net order value (NOV) declined from ₹138 to ₹114 on competitive intensity and introductory pricing for new users. “InstaHelp’s value to the platform extends beyond its own P&L: it is our highest-frequency offering and a meaningful source of new users for our core services. In this phase of category development we are prioritising market leadership. We expect losses to remain elevated for a few more quarters before they begin to come down,” it added.

data.title: SC verdict on YES Bank AT1 bonds brings relief for mutual funds, retail investors
data.description:
Nearly six years after many investors had written off any hope of recovery, the Supreme Court’s verdict on YES Bank’s ₹8,415 crore additional tier-1 (AT1) bonds has come as a major relief for mutual funds, financial institutions and retail investors.

The Supreme Court on Thursday upheld the Bombay High Court’s 2023 order that had quashed the decision of the YES Bank administrator to write down the AT1 bonds during the bank’s reconstruction in 2020. With recovery now appearing increasingly likely, mutual funds are moving swiftly to safeguard the interests of investors who were holding units in schemes exposed to the bonds at the time of the write-down.

Nippon India Mutual Fund and Kotak Mahindra Mutual Fund, which had marked down their AT1 bond holdings to zero, have temporarily halted fresh subscriptions in certain debt schemes that still hold exposure to the securities. The move is aimed at preventing new investors from benefiting from a potential windfall that rightfully belongs to existing unitholders.

“We were holding YES Bank AT1 bonds in the Nippon India Retirement Fund Wealth Creation Scheme, which was not segregated and was valued at nil after the RBI had passed an order to write them off,” Nippon India Mutual Fund said.

“We await further details on the operationalisation of the order as the valuation aspect remains unclear,” it added.

Kotak Mahindra AMC has taken a similar approach in dealing with the unexpected recovery from the AT1 bonds. Kotak Mahindra Mutual Fund had exposure of about ₹2,680 crore to the bonds, while Nippon India Mutual Fund’s exposure stood at around ₹2,150 crore.

Debt schemes

In contrast, Franklin Templeton had adopted a different approach when the crisis unfolded in March 2020. The fund house, which had exposure of about ₹590 crore to the bonds across three debt schemes, created a segregated portfolio on March 6, 2020, and issued separate units to investors who held the schemes on that date.

“Any amounts realised from these bonds will be distributed to unit-holders of the respective segregated portfolios in proportion to their holdings,” Franklin Templeton said.

According to Aakanksha Shukla, AVP-Wealth Management at Master Capital Services, investors who entered the schemes after the write-down should not be entitled to the recovery proceeds. However, without restrictions, they could potentially benefit from the recovery, which explains why some fund houses have suspended fresh subscriptions.

“The distribution of proceeds will be easier for debt funds that ring-fenced the troubled bonds through a segregated portfolio,” she said.

Apart from mutual funds, several institutional investors also stand to gain from the ruling. Sammaan Capital expects to recover about ₹662 crore, while 63 Moons Technologies could recover nearly ₹300 crore.

Relief for investors

The ruling has also brought relief to retail investors. Around 1,346 retail investors held AT1 bonds worth about ₹679 crore. Of these, 1,311 were existing YES Bank customers, including retired employees, senior citizens and homemakers, with investments aggregating around ₹663 crore.

“The Supreme Court verdict is an eye-opener for regulators that they cannot wriggle out of their responsibilities simply by writing off a problem that should have been identified at a much earlier stage,” said Kuldip Singh, a retired bank executive who invested in the AT1 bonds in 2020.

The AT1 bonds, which offered a coupon of 9-9.5 per cent and required a minimum investment of ₹1 crore, had attracted investors seeking a steady annual income. Following the Supreme Court’s ruling, many of them may finally see a recovery from an investment they had long considered lost.
